Cameroon will be without Carlos Baleba, who has withdrawn from the squad with a hamstring injury, while Christian Kofane is also unavailable with a thigh problem.

Karl Etta Eyong has not been selected despite having returned to action for Levante after his thigh injury, while Enzo Ebosse has returned to the squad for the first time since the 2022 World Cup and Bryan Mbeumo is expected to captain the side.

Andre Onana and Nouhou Tolo are among the notable omissions from Pagou's selection, with the coach explaining that he wants to assess other defensive profiles in Tolo's case.

The Cameroon coach has also included five new faces as he continues to reshape the squad, with Ryan Fosso coming in to replace the injured Baleba.

Namibia will be without Petrus Shitembi, who withdrew from the squad after sustaining an injury while playing for Malaysian club Kuching City against Selangor FC.

Absalom Iimbondi has returned to the national team for the first time since the 2024 AFCON, while Peter Shalulile is set to captain the Brave Warriors and Deon Hotto is expected to provide experience in attack.

#1646. Former Geordie Guimaraes taunts Sunderland fans as Arsenal show mark of champions

Bruno Guimarães cupped his ears and had a plastic cup thrown at him as the abuse came down from the stands. Despite the missiles, the Brazilian wore a look that made it clear he was very much enjoying his first goal in an Arsenal shirt.

Mikel Arteta has laid bare his quirky management techniques so his players are ready for any eventuality. Late meals and making the dressing room hotter are among his tricks, although nothing can prepare a player having 40,000 fans calling you a “sad Geordie b------”.

So it was a sweet moment for Guimarães, even more so after coming just after Sunderland had a penalty saved. Just 121 seconds after Enzo Le Fée had his spot kick tipped on to a post by David Raya, Guimarães was rubbing salt into the wound with a stunning long-range strike that went in off the crossbar.

Enzo Le Fée is denied by David Raya from the spot 😳🧤📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/wnoMCDVh88

Bruno Guimarães silences the Stadium of Light with a BEAUTY 🥵🚀📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zQHSSLxC3o

The former Newcastle captain gave the perfect response after being taunted his old rivals. “It was a beautiful goal,” he said. “Everyone knows my past, I had an amazing history at Newcastle. But now I’m trying to create a new history here and I have started on the right foot.”

What an important week it has been for Arsenal, who have shown their squad depth by winning in Napoli then travelling to the Stadium of Light and extending their perfect start to the season to six games.

Other teams with aspirations of the title dropped points earlier in the day, while Arteta could battle to a win with key players brought back into the team and Guimarães coming off the bench at half-time. A trip in the Champions League followed by an away game the following weekend is a barometer of where teams are, and Arsenal have sounded a warning after coming through a bruising encounter.

Régis Le Bris’s team offer a challenge that is impossible to replicate, even by the standards of Arteta’s “sabotage” to make his players uncomfortable. Fans belted out Elvis Presley and 90s anthem Ready To Go just before kick-off. Then there was the aggression that Arsenal players faced. There were complaints of elbows being aimed at Gabriel Magalhães.

Bukayo Saka scored a stoppage-time penalty to seal the win but the evening belonged to Guimarães, the £75m summer signing who has been waiting for this moment to ignite his Arsenal career.

“Everyone knows I had a difficult start through injuries in my short time. But I’m glad to be back and glad to play,” Guimarães said. “I feel very good. It was unbelievable to score a beautiful goal, beautiful moment for me and my family and I am happy.”

These are ominous signs for Arsenal’s title rivals, with Guimarães’s return to fitness adding to the midfield options. Arteta’s changes to his starting line-up restored Riccardo Calafiori and Kai Havertz – two of the in-form players in the Premier League – to the team, rather than squad players being rotated.

And his players stood up to a physical challenge. Brian Brobbey used his frame to back into the Arsenal’s centre-backs, who are unlikely to given such a tough assignment this season aside from facing Erling Haaland.

Guimarães was brought on at half-time along with Jurriën Timber, which was another sign of Arsenal mounting a strong defence of their title. With Arteta’s changes altering the pace of the game, the match turned just before the hour mark. John Brooks saw nothing in the incident that floored Gabriel at a corner, but at the next set-piece penalised Ezri Konsa for wrestling with Dan Ballard, much to Arteta’s fury.

Le Fée had earned a point against Brentford a week earlier with a penalty, but this time his finish was tipped on to the post by David Raya. “We should not talk about the save of the keeper, we should talk about what happened before that,” added Arteta.

“But I loved the save from David, the way the team reacted, the way we go again and we go against everything, but this should never happen, it’s not fair, and I am sad, very sad, in that sense.”

Raya also denied Nordi Mukiele from close range when Granit Xhaka’s expertly taken free-kick found his team-mate in front of goal. Sunderland have their own European campaign starting on Thursday and will start with confidence after pushing the champions all the way.

Brooks awarded a penalty in stoppage-time when Saka was brought down by Reinildo Mandava, who was dismissed. “I’m extremely pleased to win again. We had a really tough week, Chelsea, Napoli, winning there and now against a really tough opponent in a difficult place,” added Arteta.

Bukayo Saka wraps up all three points for Arsenal from the spot 🥶📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrLyrykwlh

Mikel Arteta launched a furious attack on referee John Brooks for awarding a penalty against Arsenal and fears similar decisions will cost his team the Premier League title.

Brooks gave a spot-kick for Ezri Konsa tussling with Dan Ballard, although Arteta accused the Sunderland centre-back of a “judo roll”.

Enzo Le Fée’s penalty was saved by David Raya, with Arsenal winning after goals from Bruno Guimarães and Bukayo Saka.

“In my opinion, that is not acceptable. I watched it 20 times,” said Arteta. “And I cannot find a way to understand how you think to give a penalty in that situation or the way the VAR has to intervene.

“I’m sad that we have to discuss something in such a beautiful game at this level. That has gravity because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship. And at this level, with all the work that we put in, this cannot happen.

“You see, it is a judo roll and it brings the player on the floor. So how can this happen? I cannot find an explanation. That’s why I’m trying to find that.”

The win rounded off a positive week for Arsenal despite Arteta’s fury at the officials.

“I’m extremely pleased to win again. We had a really tough week, Chelsea, Napoli, winning there and now against a really tough opponent in a difficult place. We had really good periods but didn’t score and after that they can suffocate you especially when they decided to be really physical and very direct and we had to overcome a situation that in my opinion was absolutely unacceptable at this level. I’m very worried and very sad because this can never be a penalty ever.

“Are you surprised? Are you surprised? No. OK.

“Ezri does nothing. Just watch it. We have a lot of cameras and VAR, and we have to take responsibility to protect the game. Today the game was unprotected and it could have cost us the game and the momentum which is a really, really serious thing,” he added.

“I’m making it very clear publicly because it’s for the game, it’s not only for Arsenal, this cannot happen at this level. We should not talk about the save of the keeper, we should talk about what happened before that.”

Guimarães’s goal was his first for Arsenal, with Arteta adding: “Beautiful, he came on, the goal, the assist, remarkable. That why we talk about the finishers and making that impact and being able to support and help the team. He was outstanding.”

Three points or not, the Arsenal manager is furious about the penalty that was awarded to Sunderland.

I’m so upset – it’s unacceptable at this level. Unacceptable. This can change the course of a season, of the championship. I’ve seen it 10 times, to make sure, because I saw it live and said ‘It’s not possible at this level it can be a penalty’. Because it’s a judo roll, that’s what it is. It cannot happen.

I’ve been in football for 27 or 28 years - it’s not a penalty in any game, in any league, in any context.

Sunderland are a really, really good team and I don’t want to take any credit away from them. It’s been extremely tough and I’m really happy that we’ve done it.

"It's not a penalty in any case, in any game, in any context, in any league" 😳Mikel Arteta reflects on Arsenal's 2-0 win over Sunderland 👀@jules_breach | 📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/2BUZILexk3

I feel very good. It was a beautiful goal and a beautiful moment for me and my family.

It’s a very good place to score! Everyone knows my history at Newcastle; now I’m trying to create more history with Arsenal.

[Is David Raya the best goalkeeper in the world?] Definitely. This guy’s an unbelievable player.

What a goal! And especially the time he scored. Coming to this place is so difficult but we dealt with it very well.

It’s a big moment, especially at 0-0 away from home, and they were on top of us at the time.

"What a goal, and especially the time that he scored" 🙌David Raya and Bruno Guimarães reflect on their win over Sunderland this evening 🤝@jules_breach | 📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mozUB0mFd8

Arsenal have won nine Premier League games in a row for the first since the Invincible season of 2003-04.

Three away games for Arsenal this season, three wins and three clean sheets. Nobody does it better. The Arsenal players will sleep well tonight because Sunderland made them work extremely hard for the three points.

The match was decided by a dramatic three-minute period early in the second half. Enzo Le Fee’s penalty was superbly saved by David Raya; then the Arsenal substitute – and former Newcastle captain – Bruno Guimares slammed a spectacular goal.

Bukayo Saka confirmed victory with an injury-time penalty. Arsenal are top of the table with 12 points out of 12; good luck trying to catch them.

Rice played a square pass to Guimaraes, lurking with intent just outside the D; he got the ball out of his feet and whipped an unstoppable curler into the top corner. What a way - and time, and place - to score your first Arsenal goal.

Bruno Guimarães silences the Stadium of Light with a BEAUTY 🥵🚀📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zQHSSLxC3o

55 min: Sunderland 0 Arsenal 0 A fantastic save from David Raya, who springs to his left and touches Enzo Le Fee’s penalty onto the post! Sensational goalkeeping!

Enzo Le Fée is denied by David Raya from the spot 😳🧤📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/wnoMCDVh88

Arsenal are furious, and that probably wouldn’t have been given last season, but clubs were told at the start of the season that wrestling would be penalised.

Gabriel goes down holding his jaw and claims he was elbowed by Ballard. VAR aren’t interested and the referee tells an irritated Gabriel to leave the field for one minute.

Konsa makes an important challenge on the relentless Brobbey, as does Gabriel on Le Fee a few seconds later. Sunderland keep pushing and Sadiki rakes a shot over the bar from the edge of the area.

Chance for Sunderland A long throw from the right isn’t cleared by Arsenal, and eventually Meunier hits a snapshot that is kicked away instinctively by David Raya. That’s a pretty good save.

Jurrien Timber and Bruno Guimaraes, who is popular in these parts, replace Ben White and Myles Lewis-Skelly.

Tzolis’s deep cross is headed back into the six-yard box by Saka. Havertz stoops towards the ball but is beaten to it by Xhaka, a crucial bit of defending and the last action of a hard-fought, goalless first half.

Ben White has a groin problem and is going to be replaced by Jurrien Timber, either now or at half-time.

Xhaka’s dangerous corner is punched back to him by Raya. He picks out Le Fee, who drags a shot wide of the near post from 20 yards. Sunderland’s belief is growing.

Angulo goes down in the Arsenal area after a challenge from the side by White. Play continues and Meunier’s speuclative shot deflects behind for a corner.

Sunderland have been terrific in this first half.

Mikel Arteta is booked for encroaching outside his technical area. He responds by sticking his thumb up at the fourth official.

Mikel Arteta receives a yellow card for stepping out of the technical area 😅📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/xDlnL1B9MY

Arsenal are yet to score from a set piece this season. Their supporters have used that fact as evidence they are not as reliant on corners as their critics say, but the truth is that it will bother Arteta and set-piece coach Nicolas Jover. This is the sort of cagey game in which Arsenal so often made the breakthrough from a set piece last season.

Sunderland break through Mukiele, who charges into space and rifles a low drive that is blocked by Gabriel on the edge of the area.

The resulting corner leads to a brief VAR check for an Arsenal penalty after a bit of a wrestling match between Calafiori and Brobbey. Nothing given.

Good save by Roefs Saka curls a cross towards Havertz, who does well to control it on the chest while facing away from goal. He waits for the ball to bounce and hooks an imaginative shot that is fingertipped over by Roefs. Good save.

Chance for Arsenal Tzolis plays a nice pass down the side of the area for Odegaard. He cuts the ball back to Havertz, who screws a first-time shot over the bar. It was a slightly awkward chance because of the angle of Odegaard’s pass.

Reinildo is booked for a foul on Saka. The home fans are getting annoyed with what they perceive as diving from some of the Arsenal attackers: “Same old Arsenal, always cheating” is the chant of choice just now. Odegaard also went down a moment ago after a foul from Angulo.

Gabriel strides forward from defence and sweeps a left-foot shot from 25 yards. It’s a good effort that fades just wide of the far post with Roefs scrambling across his line.

Sunderland will be really pleased with the first quarter. They’re defending solidly and look a threat on the break, thanks in part to some outstanding hold-up play from Brian Brobbey. Saka’s volley is the only shot on target at either end.

Chance for Sunderland Brobbey does brilliantly to hold the ball and find Le Fee, who is fouled on the left wing by Gabriel. That allows Sunderland to send the centre-backs forward - and one of them, Dan Ballard, almost opens the scoring!

Xhaka curled a sensational ball around the Arsenal defence towards the far post, where the ball bounced up awkwardly and was knocked wide by either Ballard or Mukiele, who flew in at the far post. Ballard would have had an easier chance had Mukiele not got in the way.

Chance for Arsenal Saka mishits a volley straight at Roefs from close range after running onto a penetrative pass from Rice. It wasn’t an easy ball to take on the volley - Rice hit it very firmly - but Saka would usually do better.

The pattern of the game has been established, with Arsenal dominating the ball and Sunderland picking their moments to press and then counter-attack.

Looks like it will be a good battle between Brian Brobbey and Ezri Konsa. Brobbey seems to be attaching himself to Konsa, rather than getting into a scrap with Gabriel.

Sunderland break promisingly down the right. Mukiele drives an angled low cross that only just evades Angulo at the far post.

Calafiori has a shot from 18 yards blocked after a typical run infield from left-back.

Enzo Le Fee tries to score from inside his own half. David Raya was outside the penalty area but Le Fee completely mishit the shot.

Arsenal have started well and are dominating possession. So far it’s all been in front of the Sunderland defence, but you’d expect that to change if they continue to have this much of the ball.

The champions kick off from left to right as we watch.

There’s a pulsating atmosphere at the Stadium of Light - you’d expect nothing less - and the action is about to begin.

Myles Lewis Skelly is the first England teenager to start the first four league games of a season for Arsenal since Tony Adams and David Rocastle in the 1986/87 campaign.

We’re in a congested period right now. We’re playing midweek games as well. We made four changes against Napoli, we make another four for today and we try to keep all the players connected with a high level of confidence, and with the right chemistry in and around the team.

We know how tough Sunderland made it for every opponent here [last season] and we know the beautiful atmosphere that they create, the organisation that they have and the individuals that they have. We’ll try to impose ourselves like we always do and come here and be as dominant as we’ve been and then be ready to win the game.

Arsenal’s biggest rivals are still waiting for their first win - and their first goal - of the Premier League season. Alex Connor has reaction to their 0-0 draw at home to Everton.

"For sure we can improve, and we will" 😅Mikel Arteta on Arsenal's strong start to the season 🗣️📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nDpwooZq4Y

Arsenal keeper David Raya has conceded only one goal in five matches this season, but he was beaten twice on this ground last season during a thrilling 2-2 draw.

When will Martin Zubimendi start again for Arsenal? Mikel Arteta wants to avoid a repeat of last season, when Zubimendi played more games than anyone in Europe, but it is curious that the Spaniard has not yet started a single match of this campaign. It is one thing to reduce his minutes, and another to turn him into a permanent substitute.

Zubimendi has looked quite good off the bench in recent games but has been behind Myles Lewis-Skelly and Mikel Merino in the battle to partner Declan Rice from the start. And that’s before Bruno Guimaraes, the new £75m signing, reaches full fitness.

In the thick Naples air in midweek, Declan Rice did what he always does: he kept running. Another start for the Arsenal midfielder, another 90 minutes completed and another performance of constructive passing and destructive defending. For anyone who was worried about Rice’s physical condition, it was an emphatic response.

After that Champions League victory over Napoli, Rice insisted he was ready for another marathon campaign. He made 69 appearances for club and country last season, up from 60 the previous term, and believes that is a sustainable number of games, even for an all-action midfielder such as himself. “I have shown I can do it,” he said.

The key question, though, is not whether Rice can do it, but whether he should do it. There is no doubt that his body eventually began to pay the price for his exertions last year, especially during the World Cup, and it would be reasonable for his managers to worry that his extraordinary workload might one day take a serious toll. This, after all, is a footballer who managed nerve pain in his hamstring throughout the second half of last season.

Regis Le Bris, who made 11 changes for the League Cup win over Hull in midweek, reverts to the starting XI that drew at Brentford seven days ago.

RLB's XI to take on Arsenal! ❤️👊#SUNARS pic.twitter.com/F1nXWky4Fp

Mikel Arteta has made four changes to the Arsenal team that won in Napoli during the week. Kai Havertz’s return is the headline news in Arteta’s selection, with in-form left-back Riccardo Calafiori also returning. Myles Lewis-Skelly returns to the midfield and Christos Tzolis starts.

Hello and welcome to live, minute-by-minute coverage of Sunderland v Arsenal at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland are the latest team tasked with stopping Arsenal, who have begun their title defence in formidable style: they’ve won out of three, including a dominant comeback victory against Chelsea last weekend, and look well equipped to become the first Arsenal team to retain the title since the mid-1930s.

There’s a long way to go, and Arsenal fans will remember how blisteringly they started their last two title defences in 2002-03 and 2004-05, only to ultimately fall short. But right now, they could barely be in better shape. Their fine start to the season came with a Champions League win in Naples, achieved despite a delay to their flight from London.

“I love those challenges,” said Mikel Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-seasons so when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.

“Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic and I don’t want the players, but not only the players, the staff as well, panicking. So when that happens, adapt to it.”

Arteta has tested his squad in a variety of ways. “[We have] delayed the meals, delayed the transport, taken a different route. We’ve done many things – made the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less beds... because we’re going to have to adapt to different contexts.”

So far, they’re adapting very well to the context of being the reigning champions.

#1645. Martin Odegaard sends Arsenal six clear at the top: The stylists and aesthetes will moan - but Mikel Arteta can rest easy over the international break, writes RIATH AL-SAMARRAI

By RIATH AL-SAMARRAI, CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 12:30 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 19:22 EST, 7 November 2026

Arsenal are building a wall around their precious trophy with ugly bricks. While the stylists and aesthetes among us can moan about such details, a quick glance at the league table will be sufficient for Mikel Arteta to rest easy during the international break.

There are certainly things for him to improve. Masses of them. And we can all share the disappointment that the sum of such gifted parts is often quite underwhelming. There's a relentlessness about that conversation.

But Arsenal are relentless in other ways, too. Which is to say they are finding ways to win, with this their ninth in ten games and arguably the least convincing of an unconvincing bunch.

If Manchester City weren't facing up to the possibility of an apocalyptic punishment, those performances would likely cause greater concern but it's a tangential argument. A purist's debate. And by extension it is pointless against the single factor that matters most – scoring more than the other lot.

In this case, grimy as it was, that crowning role fell to Martin Odegaard, who nudged the winner over the line in the 72nd minute after benefiting from a favourable rebound after Konstantinos Tzolakis had saved from Noni Madueke.

The latter is surfing ever faster on the wave of his current form and impressed throughout this match, but his wing play and the resilience of Arteta's back four warranted isolated praise.

Martin Odegaard secured Arsenal's fourth Premier League win in succession against Hull

The Gunners had been frustrated by the newly-promoted side before Odegaard pounced

For all of Arsenal's grumbles about the officiating, including a bizarre penalty claim for Kai Havertz in the first half, they were poor, even if most sides would trade an arm for four straight clean sheets and a healthy lead in the table.

Arsenal (4-2-3-1): Raya 6; Timber 7, Konsa 7, Gabriel 6, Calafiori 7 (Hincapie 69, 7); Rice 6 (Merino 63, 7), Guimaraes 5 (Zubimendi 89); Madueke 8, Odegaard 7, Tzolis 5 (Eze 69, 6); Havertz 5 (Gyokeres 63, 6)

Subs not used: Arrizabalaga, White, Mosquera, Lewis-Skelly

Hull (5-3-2-): Tzolakis 7; Coyle 6 (Norton-Cuffy 60, 5), Ajayi 7 (Herrington 69, 6), Egan 7, Mendy 6, Stroud 7 (Giles 75, 6); Iroegbunam 7 (Mouzakitis 75, 6), Gourna-Douath 7, Slater 7; McBurnie 6, Cho 5 (Gelhardt 60, 6)

Subs not used: Butland, Giles, Thomas, Hjerto-Dahl, Vaz

For the majority of the first 45 minutes, this game was shaped by Hull, who hadn't won since August. They had drawn five of their previous seven games and given up winning positions in four of them, but Sergej Jakirovic is doing good work. Here, he had Arteta baffled for long stretches and elements of his blueprint will have been noted by future opposition.

Jakirovic's intentions had been clear, both on the team sheet and the pitch. He kept with his default setting for a back five, but switched from a 5-4-1 to 5-3-2 and introduced Mohamed-Ali Cho to partner Oli McBurnie in attack.

It was the first time this season that Hull's manager has used a front two and dovetailed with his midweek warning that camping on the edge of their area would lead nowhere but trouble. Instead, the aim was to squeeze, suffocate and chase the champions at every turn. That worked for an hour for Leeds and it did likewise for Hull.

Inside the first 70 seconds, they had forced a corner. A moment later, John Egan outjumped Gabriel Magalhaes and headed into the side netting.

Soon enough, David Raya was forced into a save by Regan Slater. In landing a shot on target, Hull had achieved a greater threat after 18 minutes than Liverpool delivered in the entire 90 at Anfield last weekend.

It was strong stuff. And ballsy. Arsenal had space to exploit at the other end but that was contingent on having the composure to pick the right pass. For an awfully long time, that eluded them.

Christos Tzolis and Havertz each offered the limpest of protests for early penalties and Declan Rice belatedly caused some threat with a half-volley. For a while, that was as good as it got, before a third penalty appeal arrived. This one was contentious.

Arsenal were denied a penalty following a shirt pull on centre forward Kai Havertz

Mikel Arteta demands a free kick in Arsenal's favour on a frustrating afternoon in north London

Mikel Arteta warned that Arsenal must be more 'chaotic' and ruthless after wasting multiple chances in their 1-0 victory over Hull City.

Martin Odegaard's second-half strike sealed a fifth consecutive Premier League victory for the Gunners going into the international break, though his side were initially frustrated by the stubborn visitors.

'I'm delighted with the win because to go into the international break after winning is one of the best things for a coach or a player,' said Arteta.

'I think we were the better team and had enough chances to make the scoreline much bigger. We weren't efficient enough to do that.

'We need to find ways to be more efficient, sometimes even more pragmatic.

'Sometimes my feeling is that we are trying to score a perfect goal against these low blocks. We need to be much more chaotic than that, and that's it. And score much earlier because obviously that's going to change the course of the game.'

Arsenal also had a penalty shout turned down in the first period after Kai Havertz's shirt was pulled in the box by Nobel Mendy.

The decision was not given on field, though the VAR told referee Farai Hallam to look at the pitchside monitor.

Hallam announced that Havertz had been fouled, but the forward had been in an offside position.

On the incident, Arteta said: 'I haven't watched it back. I was surprised because when they sent the referee to the monitor, Benji (White) was telling me it's a clear penalty.

'So I heard now that they decided not to (give a penalty) because of the starting position of Kai, that he was offside. So I don't know what the interpretation is. I'm sure they (Pro Ref) will make that clear to understand it.

'I need to understand the decision, what is overruling what in terms of the decision making and after that I can give you an answer.'

The offence traced to a clear shirt-pull by Nobel Mendy on Havertz, with referee Farai Hallam subsequently called to the screen to check if it merited a foul. Returning to the field and engaging his microphone, he confirmed it did but added that Havertz was in an offside position. The verdict: a Hull free-kick.

A word on Hallam – he was the referee who also overruled the VAR on his Premier League debut last season. It's good to see an official who backs his own judgment, so fair play, but was he in the right?

Such is the mess engulfing the laws on offside, an argument could be put forward that, according to the regulations, the foul must take precedence over the offside as Havertz wasn't yet challenging for the ball. A counterpoint: it's an absurd law that is far too subjective.

None of which helped Arsenal, of course. Not for the first time, they were struggling to utilise their creative talents, with Rice and Odegaard swamped in the middle and their supply lines to Tzolis almost non-existent. Madueke created his own threats, but with limited support. When Havertz had a decent opening late in the half, he took one touch too many and allowed Mendy to challenge. It was bleak.

Kicking his heels on the bench was Viktor Gyokeres, who had one of his finest Arsenal performances at Slavia Prague on Wednesday. His reward for a goal and an assist was one of those soul-crushing demotions for Premier League business, and he wasn't introduced here for more than an hour.

By then, Arsenal had asserted some control. Tzolis was drawing countless fouls, including one from Lewie Coyle that ought to have drawn a second yellow card as Hull's pressure strayed closer to brute force. Their grip on a point was loosening.

First, Madueke drew a save from Tzolakis and then he forced another after skipping around Elliot Stroud and pulling the trigger. This one proved decisive because the save rebounded to Odegaard. He poached the winner.

Madueke then ought to have killed the match, but opted to round Tzolakis instead of taking on the shot when through. The keeper won that battle; Arsenal won the game. Ultimately, not much else mattered.

#1644. Stand-outs for good and bad reasons: Fan player ratings from Genoa 1-2 AC Milan

AC Milan ensured they will go into the international break in good spirits as they beat Genoa 2-1 away from home on Sunday.

Milan led by two goals inside 20 minutes after Alphadjo Cisse slotted in a cut-back from Adrien Rabiot to get his eighth of the campaign, before Christian Pulisic buried a square pass from Gonçalo Ramos after a stray pass inside the box.

Ellertsson scored with a strike from distance inside the final few minutes to make it a nervy finale, but Milan did ultimately manage to hang on for what was an important three points that moves them back into the top four.

We published our player ratings just after the full-time whistle which we would always urge you to read first, while the Italian newspapers have given their verdict on what was another game of two halves from Milan.

Starting with the positive notes, there were four players who scored a 7 or higher on average. The goal scorers Cisse (7.0) and Pulisic (7.6) were unsurprisingly two of them, but Adrien Rabiot (7.3) and Koni De Winter (7.1) were also judged to have done their bit.

Luka Modric isn’t far behind with a 6.9, while Mike Maignan follows him with a 6.8. Mario Gila got a 6.5, Sankhoun Diawara a 6.3, Diego Moreira a 6.6 and Yunus Musah a 6.1. Gonçalo Ramos (5.9) was the only starter to get below a passing grade.

The substitutes are a different story, as has often been the case. Filippo Terracciano and Ardon Jashari were both awarded a 5.5. Omari Hutchinson scored 5.0, and Pervis Estupinan was deemed worthy of a 4.6 on average.

#1643. Opinion: Liverpool defender who is 'so impressive' given last chance to save his career

Liverpool's first-team squad have been under a magnifying glass for some time now.

Ever since they finished fifth in the Premier League last term, questions have been asked about whether Liverpool actually have what it takes to start challenging for silverware again.

At the moment, it really doesn't feel like they do as they've managed to lose three games across all competitions thus far with one of those defeats coming against Fenerbahce in the Champions League.

This lack of form has forced fans to question whether the over £150 million that was spent on improving the Reds' ranks was worth it or not.

In fact, some have even started to ask for new players to be brought in to try and help them out.

However, since the club still have so many players among their ranks, they have one or two decisions to make before anything concrete can be done.

So, the fact that this Liverpool star is now down to his last chance at saving his career is rather intriguing.

Conor Bradley given six months to prove his worth to Liverpool

At the moment, Ronald Araujo has Liverpool's right-back position locked down.

The Uruguayan's natural position is as a centre-back but, thanks to the Reds' lack of depth at full-back, the 27 years old's main position has been at right-back.

This obviously isn't the first season that Araujo has played in that position as, there have also been several occasions when he was used there by Barcelona.

And, since Jeremie Frimpong is performing rather poorly, Araujo has no competition, which makes his job much easier.

However, in the New Year, Conor Bradley is expected to return from his injury which will add an extra option for Liverpool in defence.

And, since Spanish outlet Diario Sport have now confirmed that Liverpool will wait until the end of the current season to make a decision on Araujo, Bradley now only has around six months to prove why he should be the Reds' starting right-back.

"At Anfield, they are very happy with the Uruguayan, but it is a significant financial undertaking, so they don't intend to make a final decision until the end of the season, despite reports that they would like to finalize the deal now," they wrote.

"If it were today, that would be the feeling, but there's still a long season ahead and no one wants to rush into anything.

"Let's not forget that Van Dijk and Joe Gomez could leave this year, leaving the center-back position, a crucial one in England, very vulnerable. In fact, he was voted Liverpool's Player of the Month for October.

"The player is regaining his confidence thanks to consistent playing time and has scored important goals for his new team."

Conor Bradley has to take this chance and run

If Bradley wasn't constantly side-lined due to injury, Liverpool would be having no problems at right-back.

At his best, the Northern Irishman is easily one of the Premier League's best attacking right-backs with Pep Guardiola even confessing his love for him in the past.

The defender, who has been described as "so impressive" by Chris Sutton is always one of the first names on Liverpool's team sheet when available.

However, with his contract set to expire in 2029, he's got some serious work to do if he wants to extend his stay.

And, the next six months could be crucial to that.

By June 2027, Liverpool will have needed to make a decision on Araujo and whether they want to make his deal permanent or not.

If they do, there's no chance of Bradley making his way back into Iraola's plans but, if, upon his return he can outperform the Uruguayan, he could find himself back on track to getting offered a new deal.

Nobody knows what the future has in store for Liverpool but, whenever Bradley returns to action, he needs to make the most of it and save his career.

#1642. Italy vs. France: Head-to-head record and past meetings

By Jonathan O'Shea | 10 Nov 2026 17:02, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 17:05

Longstanding rivals, Italy and France have been crowned global champions six times between them, with several crucial clashes deciding which side would go on to collect silverware.

Most notably, they met in the 2006 World Cup final, which was decided on penalties after France talisman Zinedine Zidane saw red for his infamous headbutt on Marco Materazzi. After one early goal apiece - including Zidane's pinpoint free kick - football's biggest game eventually went Italy's way.

Success marked revenge for the Azzurri, following their dramatic defeat to Les Bleus in the Euro 2000 decider. On that occasion, a late strike by Sylvain Wiltord sent the final into extra time, before David Trezeguet's 'golden goal' secured another trophy for the reigning world champions.

Looking further back, Italy were traditionally the dominant side - claiming 17 wins from the first 26 meetings - but France were ascendant from 1982 on.

Inspired by Juventus star Michel Platini, Les Bleus started to pick up regular victories, and they had gone nine games unbeaten against the Azzurri before that fateful night in June 2006.

The streak notably featured a penalty shootout triumph at the 1998 World Cup on home turf, which Zidane and co would ultimately go on to win.

More recently, the pair have played out three Nations League contests: in the 2024-25 campaign, either side won 3-1 away from home.

Then, in October 2026 - with Zidane now France boss - they settled for a 1-1 draw in Paris, where Alessandro Bastoni's strike cancelled out Michael Olise's opening goal.

Oct 02, 2026: France 1-1 Italy (UEFA Nations League)

Nov 17, 2024: Italy 1-3 France (UEFA Nations League)

Sep 06, 2024: France 1-3 Italy (UEFA Nations League)

Jun 01, 2018: France 3-1 Italy (International Friendlies)

Sep 01, 2016: Italy 1-3 France (International Friendlies)

Nov 14, 2012: Italy 1-2 France (International Friendlies)

Jun 17, 2008: Italy 2-0 France (European Championship)

Sep 08, 2007: Italy 0-0 (European Championship Qualifiers)

Sep 06, 2006: France 3-1 Italy (European Championship Qualifiers)

Jul 09, 2006: Italy 1-1 France (World Cup)

#1641. Report - It's over: Liverpool finally ready to call Richard Hughes signing a failure

Liverpool are reportedly looking to replace one Richard Hughes signing. They've made an approach and are ready to rule the deal a failure.

Richard Hughes did a lot of big-money business in charge of Liverpool. He essentially oversaw a complete squad restructuring as the Reds looked to overhaul Jürgen Klopp's group and move onto something new.

Now did that work? No. Was it a good idea? No. Did the job even get completed? No, again.

Liverpool have unquestionably gone backwards since Klopp left. Their squad makes use of virtually none of the youngsters who were being brought through in 2024, while the squad also looks very imbalanced.

The reason? Most of the signings just haven't worked out. There are many, many reasons for that but sometimes they're just the wrong player. And Liverpool are willing to accept failure on at least one of them.

TeamTalk reports that Liverpool are now pushing to sign a new right-back. They claim that an approach was made for Pedro Porro, with the Reds in a group of clubs hoping to sign the Spaniard.

Whether that deal happens or not, it's a sign of the thinking at Anfield. They wanted a new right-back, just 18 months after Hughes signed Jeremie Frimpong for the role from Bayer Leverkusen.

It was a deal that always raised eyebrows. Frimpong was a right wing back in Germany and never really showed an ability to defend in a back four. He was also the sole wide player for Leverkusen and that was never going to be the case at Liverpool.

So the Reds were really asking him to be completely different. Shockingly, that didn't work and Frimpong has struggled to establish himself at the club, ultimately becoming a failed signing - despite a ridiculously unfair situation for him.

It's not his fault that Liverpool signed a player and then asked his game to be completely different. But it does mean that the team needs to move on with a player more suited for the actual role.

Liverpool are apparently trying to do that and it's a sensible move. Even if it does mean giving up on Frimpong.

#1640. Chelsea: Gus Poyet questions Xabi Alonso decision over injury-hit 22-year-old

By Ben Knapton | 10 Nov 2026 17:15

Chelsea legend Gus Poyet, in an exclusive Sports Mole interview, has questioned Xabi Alonso's decision not to start one particular Blues player more often.

The West London giants went into the international break on a sour note, having suffered a shock 1-0 loss to Sunderland in their 10th Premier League clash of the campaign.

Chelsea lie outside the top four spots in the Premier League table as a result, two points adrift of Liverpool in the final guaranteed Champions League spot and 11 behind leaders Arsenal.

Alonso deployed a midfield trio of Romeo Lavia, Moises Caicedo and Jordan Henderson to no effect at the Stadium of Light; the former two completed the full 90 minutes, while Henderson was replaced in the 87th.

However, Lavia still put in a tidy display, completing 93% of his passes and making seven recoveries, following up his stellar performance and assist against Manchester United the week before.

Lavia has largely been a second-string player with Caicedo and Henderson fully fit, though, and Poyet has been left confused at Alonso's decision to sometimes snub the Belgian.

"I really like him, and I don't know why he doesn't play more," Poyet told Sports Mole via NetBet, one of the best Boku betting sites. "As a coach, you're very specific about certain things, and perhaps there are things he doesn't do that Xabi Alonso wants his two midfielders to do.

"That might explain why he has been picking Caicedo and Henderson, but it's difficult for us to know exactly what's happening behind the scenes. I think Lavia has been impressive."

Lavia signed for Chelsea from Southampton in the summer of 2023 but has suffered from a plethora of injury problems during his three years at Stamford Bridge, missing a staggering 122 games for club and country in all tournaments.

However, the 22-year-old has thus far managed to consign his fitness woes to the past in 2026-27, making 10 appearances across all competitions and managing one goal and one assist in the process.

Lavia has started over 50% of Chelsea's Premier League games this season - six from 10 - although largely when either Caicedo and/or Henderson was unavailable to Alonso.

The Belgian was selected in each of Chelsea's first four games, all of which Henderson missed with the arm fracture he sustained at the World Cup, while Caicedo came off the bench in just one of them due to injuries of his own.

Lavia then did not start any of Chelsea's games against Brentford, Bournemouth, Everton and Tottenham Hotspur; conversely, Henderson started all four, and Caicedo three.

The ex-Southampton man was brought back into the XI against Man United, but Henderson missed the clash with the Red Devils due to illness, before Alonso's failed Lavia/Henderson/Caicedo experiment against Sunderland.

As Joao Pedro should return from injury shortly after the international break, Lavia may very well have to accept more of a backup role towards the end of the year if Caicedo and Henderson steer clear of injury and illness.

#1639. GdS: Week-long breaks and lighter sessions – Amorim bringing ‘international culture’ to Milanello

Ruben Amorim’s decisions when it comes to training have once again come under the microscope after the win over Genoa.

La Gazzetta dello Sport report that Amorim’s closing message to the players after the victory at the Marassi was music to their ears: ‘See you next Monday’. Until early next week, Milanello will remain closed, leaving the players free to recover from the early season grind.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Who knows if things might have been different had the trip to Genoa had gone differently, but the victory that put Milan back in the Champions League spot is worth the reward of a full seven days off. in the eyes of the coach.

An oddity: Serie A teams usually have a break during the international break, but not this long. It’s also worth noting that Milan’s 13 internationals are currently busy traveling around Europe and the world, while the injured players will also continue to follow their respective recovery programs.

As a reminder, Amorim gave those who were not called up by their national teams eight days off for the last international break. However, if must be remembered that it was an extended three-week one, so there was more runway before games resumed.

The extended break is not the first change introduced by Amorim and his staff. For example, the Tuesday rest granted to the team on the eve of the European trip to Bournemouth. The Rossoneri returned to the pitch on Wednesday, the same day they left for England.

This is an unusual approach compared to the traditional post-match rest schedule or a maximum of three or four days of rest during league breaks. Amorim’s training methods are also new, exemplifying the ‘international culture’ the coach seeks to instil at Milanello.

On the pitch, the sessions are never too hard or tiring. The Portuguese coach himself explained the thinking behind it, emphasising that among the many matches scheduled, the tactics and movements were essentially practiced in-game due to the limited time available between matches.

The concept of over-working players in training amidst a demanding fixture list was thought to be the cause of the many Milan injuries suffered during similar periods. Amorim has sought to rectify it, but then the list of absences for the Genoa game was long, so it all remains a work in progress.

#1638. Opinion: Wonderkid will join Andoni Iraola's squad

Andoni Iraola's time at Liverpool has been recieved differently by members of the Reds' fanbase.

Some feel like he's done a good job with what he has at his disposal and others believe that he should be doing a lot better than he is.

Right now, Liverpool are fourth in the Premier League table and have lost three games across all competitions.

And, while this is slightly better than where they ended the 2025-26 season, it's clear that there are still plenty of improvements that need to be made.

That's why so many transfer links with Liverpool have now started to emerge.

Lucca Brughmans will be joining up with Liverpool's first-team squad next season

Over the summer, four new players were added to Liverpool's first-team squad but, five were signed.

The only player who didn't join up with the Reds this season was KRC Genk's Lucca Brughmans.

The Belgian was signed by Liverpool for £30 million with fans questioning why that much was spent on a relatively unproven 18-year-old goalkeeper.

However, after being sent back on loan to Genk to get some more experience under his belt, Brughmans has brought his game on massively.

Since his return, he's make the goalkeeper spot his own with Liverpool's fans now wondering what their plans for the youngster are next season.

And now, thanks to an update from WinWin Sports, that has been made more than clear.

"Ze Maria, the agent of Brazilian goalkeeper Alisson Becker, who plays for Liverpool FC, revealed the latest developments in negotiations to renew his client's contract with the Reds, in an exclusive interview with winwin," they wrote.

"Ze Maria confirmed to our website that talks with the English club are still in their early stages, saying: 'Alisson loves Liverpool very much. We are in preliminary talks to renew the contract.'

"The agent's statements confirm what the Brazilian goalkeeper himself said, as he expressed his desire to stay at Liverpool beyond his contract, which ends at the end of the current season, confirming his happiness at the English club."

Lucca Brughmans will end up being Alisson's back-up next season

With Alisson's agent saying that they're in talks with Liverpool about extending the Brazilian's contract, it's clear that both parties want him to stay.

And, thanks to the recent performances that he's put in, it's clear why they want that to happen.

On the face of things, this is great news for Liverpool as it means that they won't have to worry about their goalkeeper for another year or two.

The Georgian was initially signed to take over from Alisson in the future but, after his 20 appearances last term, he proved that he wasn't good enough to do that.

This led to Brughmans being signed and, with how well he's been performing for Genk, there's no way that Liverpool will let him go out on loan again.

However, since Alisson is now likely to stay put, the young Belgian will have to become Iraola's number two.

So, not only does this mean that Mamardashvili will have to be moved on but, it also means that the Reds massively believe in Brughmans to meet his potential.

Here's hoping everything works out as Liverpool want it to.

#1637. Turkey vs Belgium - prediction, team news, lineups

By Oliver Thomas | 10 Nov 2026 17:50, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 22:34

Seeking to strengthen their hopes of qualifying for the UEFA Nations League quarter-finals, Belgium travel to Gursel Aksel Stadium in Izmir to face Turkey in their penultimate League A Group 1 fixture on Thursday evening.

While the hosts’ fate is all but sealed, the visitors currently sit third in the group and are playing catch up behind both France and Italy heading into their remaining two matches this week.

After finishing third in their group behind both France and Italy in the 2024-25 Nations League, Belgium are at risk of suffering the same fate this year having won two and lost two of their opening four matches in League A.

The September/October international break was the first time the Red Devils were in action under new head coach Mark van Bommel, who saw “beautiful things” from his players despite suffering a heavy 4-1 defeat to France on matchday four.

Sitting one point behind Italy and four adrift of leaders France, Belgium know that a defeat in Turkey and an Azzurri win over Les Bleus would end their hopes of securing a top-two finish in the group. However, collecting three points on Thursday would ensure that the group will be decided on the final matchday.

Ranked eighth in the world by FIFA, Belgium will take comfort from having already beaten both Turkey and Italy in the Nations League without reply, winning 2-0 away against the latter before beating the former 3-0 on home soil courtesy of a Kevin De Bruyne brace and a strike from record goalscorer Romelu Lukaku.

Having lost only one of their last six encounters with Turkey across all competitions, the Red Devils head to Izmir confident of avoiding consecutive international defeats for the first time since March 2025.

Turkey are beginning a new era under former international midfielder Sergen Yalcin, who was appointed head coach last month following the dismissal of Vincenzo Montella after three years in charge.

Montella’s reign came to an end following Turkey’s nightmare start to their Nations League campaign, losing each of their opening four matches by an aggregate score of 11-2; this poor run of form came after they were dumped out in the 2026 World Cup group stage over the summer.

Yalcin returns to management just six months after leaving his role with Besiktas, who finished fourth in the Turkish Super Lig last season. The 54-year-old has called for “unity and togetherness” to ensure that the national team can “experience very successful days from now on”.

Ranked 31st in the world by FIFA, Turkey cannot qualify for the Nations League quarter-finals, but they still have a slim chance of avoiding direct relegation from League A, needing points from their final two matches to edge out Serbia and Czechia as one of the two best fourth-placed teams across all groups in League A.

To avoid finishing rock bottom of the group, Turkey must beat Belgium by at least four goals on Thursday to overtake them on the head-to-head tiebreaker, secure another victory against France on matchday six, and hope Belgium drop points in their final game against Italy.

The Crescent-Stars, who won four consecutive home matches prior to their two Nations League home losses this term, are unbeaten in three meetings with Belgium on their own turf, winning 3-2 in their most recent home encounter in a Euro 2012 qualifier.

Turkey are still having to cope without star attacker Kenan Yildiz, who requires further treatment to a metatarsal fracture at club level with Juventus, while Kerem Akturkoglu, Irfan Kahveci, Samet Akaydin and Altay Bayindir are among those left out of the squad after being called up last month.

Centre-back Abdulkerim Bardakci is suspended for the clash with Belgium, while Zeki Celik, Merih Demiral, Ozan Kabak, Salih Ozcan and Can Yilmaz Uzun are all just one booking away from a ban.

Key creative midfielder Arda Guler, who scored and assisted in Real Madrid's La Liga win over Valencia last weekend, is expected to start in an advanced central role, while 108-cap Hakan Calhanoglu will surpass Tuncay (22) to become Turkey third-highest goalscorer if he finds the net on Thursday.

As for Belgium, goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois continues to take a break from international duty, while Van Bommel has revealed that AC Milan defender Koni De ‌Winter refused to be called up because he was unhappy with his lack of game time last month.

Genk’s Josue Kongolo, 20, has subsequently earned his first senior call-up and will battle with Arthur Theate, Brandon Mechele and Nathan Ngoy for a place in the heart of the defence.

Chelsea midfielder Romeo Lavia is suspended, while Lukaku, Ngoy, Joaquin Seys, Nicolas Raskin and Dodi Lukebakio are all one yellow card away from a ban.

Midfield stars De Bruyne and Youri Tielemans are both back from a ban they served on matchday four last month, while winger Jeremy Doku has returned to the squad and is likely to start after missing the previous international window through injury.

Cakir; Celik, Kabak, Demiral, Kadioglu; Ozcan, Calhanoglu; Aydin, Guler, Yilmaz; Gul

Lammens; Castagne, Ngoy, Mechele, De Cuyper; Raskin, Tielemans; Lukebakio, De Bruyne, Doku; De Ketelaere

Turkey will be desperate for an immediate manager bounce under Yalcin as they look to kick-start their survival bid, but Belgium are rightfully regarded as favourites following their comfortable three-goal victory over the Crescent-Stars last month.

Boosted by the return of a few key players, the Red Devils should possess enough firepower to breach a leaky Turkish backline and are well-placed to claim three important points on the road.

#1636. Much-improved Newcastle stop the rot with a 1-1 draw at Fulham - but 'slapstick' defending and wasteful finishing will leave Matthias Jaissle rueing a missed opportunity, writes CRAIG HOPE

Published: 12:52 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 19:24 EST, 7 November 2026

Just when Newcastle looked set for victory after Jacob Murphy had borrowed Amar Dedic's bow to arrow them into a late lead, they turned the weapon on themselves.

After a week in which Dedic, Bosnia's answer to Robin Hood, had made headlines when pursued by police for wandering around the Northumberland countryside with his hunting gear, the Geordies were ready to rob the good folk of west London after Murphy found the target ten minutes from time.

Less than three minutes later and they were picking the arrow from their own foot. William Osula failed to protect possession and allowed Fulham to enter the penalty area. Then, with the ball bouncing around the goalmouth, it was home substitute Rodrigo Muniz who pounced to punish Newcastle's scruffy defending.

'Slapstick', visiting boss Matthias Jaissle later called it.

The German also said that his team deserved to win but you got the impression he was relieved to emerge without defeat, especially as the performance was improved on the back of a run of four losses in five.

Newcastle's second-half spirit also showed a response to a week of noise centred on dressing-room unrest, not to mention Dedic's police drama.

Jacob Murphy thought he had won it for Newcastle after scoring late on at Craven Cottage

Rodrigo Muniz netted moments later after sloppy defending from Newcastle, earning a 1-1 draw

Matthias Jaissle's side were much improved but must cut out the errors to win matches

And Jaissle was right in that his team could have left with three points had master archer Harvey Barnes not missed a hat-trick of chances.

Fulham (4-2-3-1): Leno 7; Castagne 6 (Tete 77, 5), Affengruber 6, Bassey 6, Robinson 5; Berge 6, Charles 6; Bobb 6 (Sessegnon 78, 6), King 7 (Palacios 72, 5), Iwobi 6; Garcia 4 (Muniz 65, 8)

Subs not used: Lecomte, Andersen, Hugo Larsson, Manuel Angel, Kevin

Newcastle (4-2-3-1): Hornicek 7; Dedic 6, Thiaw 7 (Schar 85, 6), Burn 7, Hall 6; Nico Gonzalez 5 (Miley 61, 6), Steur 7 (Fernandez-Pardo 74, 5); Murphy 8, Wissa 6 (Willock 61, 5), Barnes 6; Osula 5 (Elanga 85)

Subs not used: Pope, Livramento, Botman, Bazoumana Toure

The winger is the player to whom they'd want those opportunities to fall, too. But twice before half-time, when denied by Bernd Leno from close range, and then again when lashing wide after the break, he failed to give his side the advantage.

Murphy corrected his team-mate's finishing when capitalising on a loose pass from Cesar Palacios and slamming into the bottom corner from 25 yards, but that joy was short-lived.

In truth, there hadn't been much joy to behold all afternoon. The draw keeps both sides in the bottom half of the table, and that is where they will likely stay.

The first half, in particular, had very strong last-on-Match-of-the-Day vibes.

Newcastle thought they had a 33rd-minute lead when Dan Burn stole in at the near post to flick home from Murphy's low cross.

What the officials had spotted at the far post was linebacker Yoane Wissa pinning defender Timothy Castagne, and so playing Burn onside. It was the right call, even if Jaissle disagreed

'I learned that word here, a 'soft' decision. In my eyes, it was not right,' he said. 'But I was pleased with our complete commitment and togetherness.

'We grew through the game and that was excellent, something to build on. We showed the fundamentals.'

Dedic twice came close to creating goals with teasing crosses from the right, and you wondered if he would have mimicked Barnes' trademark archer celebration had they been converted.

He was kept away from the media post-match, but Jaissle did say: 'He played well, right? It (the bow & arrow incident) didn't affect him. He was not aware of the rules. We don't need to make a big deal out of it.'

Fulham's Josh King was included in Thomas Tuchel's England squad on Friday, the club's first Three Lions call-up in eight years. He, however, now needs a scan on a tight groin before learning if he's fit enough to feature.

Did the 19-year-old play like a would-be England international? He was his side's best player in the first half, even if that was a low bar to hurdle. One volley would have raised the roof had it gone in, so sweet was the connection from 20 yards. Lukas Hornicek needed every inch of his 6ft 6in frame to dive and save. And that, too, was a recurring theme, Newcastle's reliance on the big Czech to bail them out when giving up chances.

Like Newcastle, however, Fulham simply weren't good enough to take them.

#1635. Next Man United manager: Five signings Mauricio Pochettino could make in January to boost Red Devils squad

By Matt Law | 10 Nov 2026 18:04, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 18:09

Mauricio Pochettino is the favourite to become the new Manchester United head coach, with Michael Carrick expected to lose his job at Old Trafford this week.

Man United's director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada are expected to recommend to co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, in a meeting on Wednesday, to remove Carrick as head coach in order to move in a new direction.

Pochettino has emerged as the red-hot favourite for the position, with the Argentine potentially leaving his managerial job with the United States to take the role at Old Trafford.

Here, Sports Mole looks at five players who could be signed by the 20-time English champions in January to hand the squad a much-needed boost for the second half of the season.

Man United desperately need to boost their defence, and Bassey is believed to be on Man United's radar for the January transfer window.

The 26-year-old only has a contract with Fulham until the end of the campaign, and it is not impossible to imagine him leaving Craven Cottage in the January transfer window.

Bassey fits the bill for Man United given his age and the fact that he is proven in the Premier League, making 104 appearances in the competition for Fulham.

Man United need some pace and power in the middle of their defence, and Bassey would also bring European experience, having played in the Champions League for Ajax, and the Europa League for both the Dutch club and Rangers.

The Red Devils would not have to break the bank to sign Bassey, and he could be a very interesting January option for the 20-time English champions.

Collins, 25, is another centre-back allegedly being monitored by Man United, with the club said to be huge admirers of the Republic of Ireland international.

The centre-back has been restricted to just six appearances for Brentford this season due to injury problems, but he made his return against Brighton & Hove Albion last time out.

Collins has made 154 Premier League appearances for Brentford, Wolverhampton Wanderers and Burnley, while he has also been capped on 40 occasions by his country.

At 6ft 5in, Collins would bring a serious presence to the middle of the Man United defence, while he is also excellent on the ball, boasting the ability to begin attacks from the back.

Collins has a contract with Brentford until the summer of 2029, with the option of a further two years, but Man United would be a difficult club to turn down.

Ait-Nouri was linked with a move to Man United in the latter stages of the summer transfer window, but he ultimately remained with Man City.

It has been a frustrating campaign for the 25-year-old, who has been restricted to just four appearances in all competitions, coming up with three assists.

Ait-Nouri has not made a single appearance in the Premier League this season, but he has featured on 152 occasions in the competition for Wolves and Man City, in addition to playing eight times in the Champions League.

Man United need to bring in a new left-back, and Ait-Nouri fits the bill, as he has huge experience at this level, in addition to much-needed pace and energy in a wide area.

It is not happening for Ait-Nouri at Man City at this moment in time, but he is admired by Man United and could stay in Manchester to reignite his career.

Real Sociedad's Oskarsson has emerged as an interesting January option for Man United, with the club said to be huge admirers of the Iceland international.

The 22-year-old could be available for a fee in the region of €20m (£16.7m), making him a bargain signing, and he would give Pochettino a genuine centre-forward option.

Benjamin Sesko is out until at least January with a shin injury, while Joshua Zirkzee does not have a long-term future with the 20-time English champions.

Oskarsson, who has been compared to Erling Haaland, has scored six goals in 14 appearances for Real Sociedad during the 2026-27 campaign, including four in 10 league outings, while he has struck twice in four Europa League fixtures.

The forward has scored 23 goals in 76 appearances for La Real in all competitions and is also allegedly being tracked by Tottenham Hotspur.

Mateta's contract with Palace is due to expire at the end of the season, and it is incredibly difficult to imagine him signing an extension at this stage.

The Frenchman has scored 63 goals and registered 14 assists in 208 appearances for Palace in all competitions, including 50 goals and nine assists in 166 Premier League matches.

Man United are known admirers of the 29-year-old, and he would provide their attack with a much-needed boost in the middle of the campaign.

Mateta is likely to be available for a cut-price fee in the winter market given his contract situation.

It has been a frustrating campaign to date for the striker due to injury and suspension, but he has proven himself in England's top flight, in addition to scoring twice in seven caps for France.
