#1531. Jeff Ekhator back in Juventus group training after injury nightmare

Jeff Ekhator has finally rejoined his Juventus teammates on the training pitch. The young striker, signed from Genoa in the summer, took part in a full group session at the Continassa on Friday for the first time since a run of muscle problems that has so far kept him out of every competitive game in black and white.

His return gives Luciano Spalletti one more name to consider in a week when the squad has been kept together at the training centre ahead of Sunday’s visit of Napoli.

Juventus announced the permanent deal on 1 July, and Football Italia put the fee at €16m plus add ons. The 19 year old has barely been available since.

According to Gianluca Di Marzio, who credits Sky Sport Italia with the news, his troubles began in the very first friendly of pre-season against Basel. He recovered in time to be named in the squad for the second Serie A round against Parma, where he stayed on the bench, but broke down again a few days later and has spent roughly two further months on the sidelines.

Di Marzio describes the forward as fully recovered, and Friday’s session with the rest of the group was his first since that setback.

Jeff Ekhator signs for Juventus from Genoa on a permanent deal! ⚪️⚫️ Welcome to the club, Jeff! 🙌

Nobody should expect Ekhator to be rushed into the starting eleven after so long without match practice. Football Italia sees him more as an extra option from the bench, giving Spalletti a third centre forward alongside Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani.

That alone matters for a side that has struggled for goals. Juventus have scored 11 times in nine league games, and the 2-0 defeat at Genoa on Wednesday, covered in our report on Spalletti’s apology, left them level on 14 points with Napoli.

The timing of his comeback is notable. After the Genoa loss, chief executive Giovanni Carnevali met the players and the coach, and Spalletti then decided to keep the squad together at the training ground until kick off, as explained in our piece on the Juventus retreat.

Napoli come to the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 1 November for Matchday 10, with kick off at 20:45 local time. According to the club’s own match notes, it is the first time since April 2021 that the two sides meet on the same number of points in Serie A.

Whether Ekhator makes the matchday squad will become clear when Spalletti names his group. Either way, having a fit young striker back in training is a rare piece of good news for Juventus this week.

Sources: Gianluca Di Marzio, Football Italia, Juventus

Sergio Lattanzi has followed Juventus since the days of the Trap, when Serie A felt like the centre of the football world and the Bianconeri were its undisputed rulers. Born and raised in Turin, he developed an early obsession with the tactical patterns that made Juventus so difficult to beat, and that curiosity never left him. He watches matches with a notepad nearby and a tendency to rewind passages of play more times than anyone around him considers reasonable.

#1530. Repubblica: Milan and Real Madrid watching as Napoli star McTominay stalls on contract

Scott McTominay’s Napoli future is in doubt, and a report has named AC Milan among the surprise potential suitors.

In a Napoli side that appears to have lost its way, one of the few lights leading the way remains McTominay. Despite a season that started on the wrong foot and a heart condition (now resolved), the Scot has five goals in 11 games this season across Serie A and the Champions League.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Massimiliano Allegri’s team is going through a tough time, and the former Manchester United player himself has had some tough nights. As La Repubblica (via Calciomercato.com) report, Napoli fans are beginning to worry about where things are heading.

The 29-year-old McTominay is at a turning point in his career, one which has been revitalised since his arrival at Napoli and the Scudetto won under Antonio Conte. His current contract with the Neapolitans expires in 2028, but negotiations for a renewal have stalled.

Fabrizio Romano reported that Napoli remain confident in the possibility of reaching an agreement over an extension, but the uncertainty currently surrounding the project, the bad results and doubts about the club’s future are forcing him to evaluate.

La Repubblica add that the discussions have even stalled after positive steps were taken in September. McTominay and his representatives want to better understand the Azzurri’s vision moving forward before finalising a new agreement.

Sky Switzerland journalist Sacho Tavolieri reported that the former Manchester United man’s agent has already held discussions with several English clubs. Napoli have not completely ruled out a possible sale, and the figure would be €25-30m.

His contract is currently worth €4.5m net per season. Napoli would like to extend it until 2030 with a salary increase, but they are unwilling to accept the Scotsman’s demands, who has requested around €7-8m net per season.

According to La Repubblica, at the end of the season McTominay and Napoli will sit down to discuss the terms of the new contract, once the club’s plans are clearer. Several clubs are interested though and are watching closely.

Aston Villa and Manchester United enquired in the summer. In the coming weeks, Real Madrid and AC Milan will also be keeping a close eye on the developments surrounding McTominay.

The Rossoneri are currently well-stocked in midfield with Luka Modric, Adrien Rabiot, Yunus Musah, Ardon Jashari plus options like Ruben Loftus-Cheek and the young Christian Comotto. However, with Amorim at the helm, the prospect of profound change is never far away.

#1529. England vs. Croatia: How to watch, date, time, live stream and TV channel for UEFA Nations League clash

By Darren Plant | 11 Nov 2026 11:22

England and Croatia return to UEFA Nations League action on Thursday night.

The two teams are competing in Group 3 of League A as they bid to bolster their hopes in this competition and their chances of Euro 2028 qualification.

Here, Sports Mole provides details of how to tune into the contest.

The Nations League match will kick off at 7.45pm, UK time, on Thursday.

England against Spain will take place at Wembley Stadium, which boasts a capacity of 90,000

This is the first time that England have squared off against Croatia at this particular venue since their opening match of Euro 2020, which was held in June 2021.

The Nations League match will be shown live on ITV1 and STV for viewers in the UK.

ITV's streaming service ITVX will be showing the Nations League match from Wembley live, and it can be accessed on phones, computers and games consoles.

In Scotland, the STV Player will provide similar levels of access.

Action from the game will be uploaded to the ITV Sport YouTube channel and itv.com shortly after the full-time whistle at Wembley Stadium.

The @itvfootball X account will also post goals, red cards and other notable incidents.

When England lost to Spain on matchday one, Thomas Tuchel would have accepted that they needed four successive victories to remain in the hunt for top spot.

Not only have the Three Lions recorded three wins in a row, their 7-0 triumph in Croatia has essentially ensured that England will finish second in a worst-case scenario.

There is currently a 21-goal difference between England and Croatia in the table. For Croatia to remain as contenders for the runners-up spot, they must win by at least a 7-0 scoreline at Wembley.

Realistically-speaking, Croatia will be focused on avoiding relegation to League B of the UEFA Nations League. That would be achieved if they can avoid defeat at Wembley and Spain beat Czech Republic.

If Spain overcome Czech Republic in Prague, England would need to match the result of the world champions to take the race for first position to Sunday's showdown in Madrid.

#1528. Juventus and Napoli meet level on 14 points as Allegri ban and Lobotka injury bite

Juventus host Napoli at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday with both sides on 14 points and both short of key figures. Spalletti is missing seven players, while Napoli lose their suspended coach and their midfield organiser Lobotka.

Juventus and Napoli go into Sunday’s Serie A Matchday 10 meeting at the Allianz Stadium level on points. Both benches will look different. Napoli will be without their head coach, with assistant Landucci on the bench. Spalletti is still missing seven players.

Allegri was sent off in Napoli’s 3-3 home draw with Roma. Serie A’s sporting judge then punished him for disrespectful remarks to the match officials. The ban covered the trip to Monza on 28 October and now the visit to Juventus. Napoli first announced an appeal. Allegri dropped it, saying he feared the ban could rise to four matches. The suspension is now final.

Napoli also lost Lobotka at Monza. He was stretchered off just after the 15th minute following a challenge with Mangas. The club’s medical update found damage to the tibiofibular syndesmosis in his left ankle, without instability. He also has a low-grade injury to the anterior talofibular ligament. He has started rehabilitation, with Napoli aiming for a return against Fiorentina in the Coppa Italia on 16 December. Badiashile and Neres are also injured.

The Juventus list is longer. Yildiz is expected back in early December after a foot operation, Sky Sport Italia reported. Thuram, who had knee surgery, is due back in early 2027. Locatelli is out until 2027 after a lateral meniscus operation. Grabara, with a right-knee ACL injury, is effectively out for the season.

Nico González (right soleus), Çelik (left hamstring) and Conceição (shoulder dislocation) are all expected back after the international break. There is one return. Young forward Ekhator is available again.

Juventus arrive after an uneven run. Lazio won 3-0 away at Juventus on 18 October. Spalletti’s side then won at Lecce on 25 October, with goals from McKennie and Douglas Luiz. Genoa won the next game through first-half goals from Ehizibue and Baldanzi. Koopmeiners hit the crossbar in stoppage time.

After the Genoa defeat, chief executive Carnevali held a long meeting with the squad. He told them to change course straight away, especially in their mentality. Spalletti then announced the squad would stay together from Friday evening until the Napoli game. The club wants the response to come from the players on the pitch rather than from a change of coach. John Elkann still backs Spalletti, and the coach has no intention of giving up, according to Tuttosport.

🗣️ "There’s only one way to win games: you have to want it more than your opponents"

The Bianconeri host Napoli at the Allianz Stadium on Serie A Matchday 10, and coach Luciano Spalletti previewed the action ⤵️

🗞️ https://t.co/8lyakgqdxW#JuveNapoli pic.twitter.com/KGApOET8on

— JuventusFC 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@juventusfcen) October 31, 2026

The fixture also brings Spalletti back against Napoli, the club he won the title with. The last meeting, in January 2026 at the Allianz Stadium, ended 3-0 to Juventus. Jonathan David, Kenan Yildiz and Filip Kostić scored. A win on Sunday would lift Juventus clear of a direct rival. Spalletti’s pre-match press conference is set for Saturday 31 October at 17:00, the day before kick-off.

#1527. Slovenia vs Switzerland - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 11 Nov 2026 11:29, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 11:31

Switzerland will be bidding to secure first spot in Group B1 and automatic promotion to League A when they continue their UEFA Nations League campaign on Friday against Slovenia.

National Team have been perfect in the 2026-27 tournament, collecting 12 points from four matches, and they will be facing a Slovenia side that are second in the section.

Slovenia boast a record of two wins, one draw and one defeat from their four matches in Group B1, with seven points representing a solid return.

Bostjan Cesar's side are three points ahead of third-placed Scotland and five behind the leaders Switzerland, demonstrating the need for them to secure a win on Friday night.

Slovenia, as it stands, are in a promotion playoff spot, but they could still finish first or third, with two games left to play, heading to North Macedonia after this one.

The hosts picked up four points from their first two games in the section, drawing 0-0 with Scotland before recording a 2-0 win over North Macedonia; a 2-1 defeat to Switzerland followed, and they then recorded a 2-1 victory over Scotland last time out.

Slovenia have only won two of their previous 12 matches against Switzerland in all competitions, with their last success over Friday's opponents coming in October 2014.

Switzerland are certain of a top-two spot in the section, but it would be a shock if they passed up first position and automatic promotion to League A from such a strong position.

National Team are top of Group B1 on 12 points, and they have been impressive in the tournament, opening up with a 3-0 win over North Macedonia, before recording a 3-0 victory over Scotland in their second away game in the section.

Murat Yakin's side then won back-to-back home fixtures in October, beating Slovenia 2-1 and North Macedonia 3-0 to take complete control of the section.

Switzerland were beaten by Argentina in the quarter-finals of the 2026 World Cup, but they have won eight of their last nine matches and will once again be the favourites here.

National Team will finish their Group B1 campaign at home to Scotland on November 16.

Slovenia will be without the services of two players through suspension on Friday, with David Zec and Erik Janza missing due to an accumulation of yellow cards.

Benjamin Sesko is another notable absentee for the home side; the Manchester United striker remains unavailable with a shin injury and is not expected back until early 2027.

Swansea City's Zan Vipotnik started through the middle against Scotland last time out, and the 24-year-old is expected to keep hold of his spot in the XI for this match.

Switzerland, meanwhile, have no suspension issues, although a booking for Michel Aebischer in this match would see him ruled out of the team's final group fixture.

There are not expected to be any major surprises in the away side's lineup for this match, with Remo Freuler, Johan Manzambi and Dan Ndoye among those set to be in the starting side.

Meanwhile, there should be a spot through the middle for Zeki Amdouni, who has scored 14 times in 37 appearances for his country.

Oblak; Karnicnik, Brekalo, Bijol, Drkusic, Kuzmic; Matko, Zabukovnik, Gnezda Cerin, Sturm; Vipotnik

Kobel; Britschgi, Elvedi, Akanji, Rodriguez; Freuler, Manzambi; Sow, Rieder, Ndoye; Amdouni

This is shaping up to be a fascinating battle in the Nations League; it would not be a surprise to see the points shared, but we just have a feeling that Switzerland could edge a close match to continue their perfect record in the 2026-27 tournament.

#1526. Liberali praises Cisse and looks back on Milan decision: “It wasn’t easy”

Mattia Liberali has looked back on his decision to leave AC Milan and to snub rejoining them, insisting he has ‘no regrets’.

After making his way through the youth sector, Liberali burst onto the scene in the 2024 summer preseason under Paulo Fonseca. He also made his first senior start under the Portuguese coach, but then found chances hard to come by and opted to leave the following year.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

On Tuesday afternoon, Liberali spoke in the press conference room at Coverciano – the Italian national team headquarters – alongside Alphadjo Cisse. The pair were team-mates at Catanzaro last season and could have reunite at Milan, but the former chose to head to Cesc Fabregas’ Como.

Speaking to the reporters present, Liberali once again commented on why he wanted to leave Milan in the first place to head to the Serie B side. His words were relayed by MilanNews.

Is there any regret about how things ended with Milan?

“No regrets. You have to make decisions with confidence and not look back. I’m very happy for Cisse, who’s succeeding. It wasn’t easy leaving AC Milan, but it’s always important to look forward.”

What was it like making the jump to Como?

“It’s not easy to go from Serie B to the intensity of Serie A and the Champions League. Aquilani? I’m sorry about his dismissal, he helped me so much last year. I’ll write to him in the next few days, I’m sorry he wasn’t able to make his mark at Sassuolo.”
